transcriberDoubts: p.5 example-2: Diagram: the Black King is read on the King's file, fourth row from the top (FEN e5). The page image is small and the row is the least certain part of this diagram (one row lower, e4, cannot be fully excluded by eye).

p.5 example-2: Branch structure: the text gives 2...K — B 5 and 3...K — B 6 as 'if' moves, then says 'Now the ending may continue: 4...K — B 7', which follows on from them. I put 2...K-B5, 3 R-R5, 3...K-B6, 4 R-R4 into main (the sequence that ends in mate on move 11) and made 2...K — K 4 (line a) and 3...K — Kt 5 (line b) the side lines.

p.8 example-4: '(if K — R 4, K — B 4 and mate next move)': neither Black's next move nor the mating move is printed. Line b stops at 6. K-B4 and 'and mate next move' is kept as a comment, not as moves.

p.8 example-4: The two bracketed alternatives carry no move numbers in the book. Read from their place in the text: 'Should Black play K — Kt 5' replaces Black's 4th move (4... K-Kt4) and 'if K — R 4' replaces Black's 5th move (5... K-R5).

p.27 example-17: Diagram: the Queen on White's Q 1 (FEN d1) looks solid dark in the page image, like a Black Queen standing on a white square, unlike the outlined White Queens in the other diagrams. I transcribed it as it looks (q), so rank 1 reads R2q1RK1. It may be a wrong piece printed in the book or an effect of the small image; if it is a White Queen, rank 1 is R2Q1RK1.

p.26 example-17: 'Black can now either reply with the identical move or play ...': the alternative is given in words only, no move is printed. Line a is written as 2... Kt-KB3 (the same move as White's 2 Kt — K B 3).

p.26 example-17: 'The Bishop could also have been played to B 4' (line b, written 4. B-B4) and '(... if he also plays B — Kt 5.)' on page 27 (line d, written 7... B-Kt5) carry no move numbers; the numbers are read from where the sentences stand.
p.27 example-17: 'He is now forced to play 7...B × Kt' is given in the prose, not in the move column; I added it to main as Black's 7th move.

p.27 example-17: Threats that are named but not played at a stated point are kept in comments only, not as lines: 'with Kt × P to follow' (page 26) and 'a combination to win quickly by Kt — Q 5' (page 27).
p.25 example-17: The section's opening paragraph says 'two moves, 1 P — K 4 or 1 P — Q 4', before Example 17 begins. It is kept in the first comment only; 1 P — Q 4 is not made a line.
p.29 example-18: 'prefers the text move to Kt — Q B 3' carries no move number; line a is written as 3... Kt-QB3 (in place of 3... Kt-Q2).
p.30 example-18: Black's 7th move is printed 'P — B 3' in the move column, while the prose just above it calls the same move 'P — Q B 3'. Transcribed as printed in the column (7... P-B3).

p.30 example-18: Threats that are named but not played at a stated point are kept in comments only, not as lines: 'White threatened Kt — Kt 5', 'White threatens R — Q 1, to be followed by P × P', and 'would finally force him to play P × P'.

p.31 example-19: 'If Kt — B 3; Q — Q Kt 3 wins a Pawn.' carries no move numbers. Read from its place (directly under 6 B — Q B 4, Q — B 3) as Black's alternative on move 6, answered by White's 7th: line b = 6... Kt-B3, 7. Q-QKt3.

p.32 example-19: 9. Kt-Q5 is not in the move column. It comes from the prose under the diagram ('has a chance of obtaining an advantage quickly by playing Kt — Q 5 anyway') and I appended it to main as White's 9th move. 'To prevent Kt — Q 5.' is kept as a comment only.
p.32 example-19: Diagram: the Queen on Black's K B 3 (FEN f6) is read as a Black Queen. It stands on a shaded square and at this image size its colour is not certain.

p.33 example-20: Diagram: there are two small marks, one on Black's K R 2 (FEN h7) and one on White's Q R 4 (FEN a4). Both are read as specks on the page, not pieces: h7 and a4 are transcribed empty, with the Black Pawn on h6.
p.33 example-20: 'Black should have recaptured with the Pawn.' is given in words only, no move is printed. Line a is written as 1... PxP.

p.34 example-21: Move numbering: Black moves first from the diagram ('suppose he plays Kt — K B 3 instead') and the book gives that move no number; White's reply is printed as move 1. So that the sequence can be replayed I wrote Black's opening move as '0... Kt-KB3' and the recommended 'P — K 3' as '0... P-K3' (line a). The '0...' is mine, not the book's.

p.34 example-21: 'Nor does B — R 5 help matters, because of 2 Q × B': the move is printed 'B — R 5' and is transcribed as printed (line c, 1... B-R5). It may be a misprint or the square may be counted from White's side; I did not correct it. It carries no number; read as a Black reply on move 1 in the Kt — K 5 line.

p.34 example-21: 'the threat being of course if B × Q; 2 B × P mate' and '1... B — K 3 leaves Black with the inferior position' are read as Black replies to the alternative 1 Kt — K 5 (lines b and d), not to 1 B × P ch. 'Kt — K 5' itself carries no number; read as White's alternative on move 1.
